transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I can’t shake this feeling that work isn’t safe anymore. And I keep thinking I’m somehow damaged now—like the capable person who got promoted isn’t really there anymore.
Did a specific event happen at work that made you feel it is no longer safe?
I’m not sure there was one specific event. It’s more that I started feeling that way, and I can’t really point to a single thing that caused it.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most days?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling depressed most days, exactly.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?
Yeah, I think so. I’ve pulled back from mentoring and the women-in-tech leadership events I used to do. I just don’t feel steady or reliable enough to show up the way I used to.
Aside from work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday areas of your life, such as your family, health, or finances?
Not constantly, no. I mean, I have normal things I think about, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time about my family, health, or finances.
When you are around coworkers or participating in these events, do you find yourself intensely afraid of being judged, scrutinized, or embarrassing yourself?
I haven’t really noticed being intensely afraid of that. I do feel less able to participate lately, but it’s not mainly because I think people are judging me or that I’ll embarrass myself.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately?

Yeah. Most nights I’m lying awake replaying little things from work, or I’ll jolt awake from dreams where I’m hiding under the conference table again. Even if I get six or seven hours, I wake up feeling like I never really powered down.
You mentioned dreaming about hiding under the conference table again—did a frightening event actually happen where you had to hide like that?

Yes. Things like the badge scanner beeping, heavy footsteps in a hallway, even a late-night deployment alert can suddenly put me right back in that office. My chest gets tight, and I see the guard on the floor like it’s happening again.
How long have you been having these dreams and reactions to reminders of that event?
Since the break-in, during that overnight deployment—about two years and four months now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (ICD-10 F43.1) following exposure to a traumatic break-in at work. She exhibits recurrent intrusive re-experiencing and physiological reactivity triggered by environmental cues, distressing nightmares, persistent negative beliefs regarding safety and self-worth, anhedonia with social/professional withdrawal, and marked sleep disruption lasting over two years.

confirmed_symptoms: Distressing nightmares of hiding under the conference table during the break-in
Intrusive flashbacks and acute physiological reactivity (tight chest, visual re-experiencing) triggered by sounds resembling the event
Pervasive sense of threat and persistent negative self-concept ('damaged')
Diminished interest and withdrawal from professional mentoring and leadership events
Significant sleep disturbance, frequent awakenings, and non-restorative sleep
